questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Palau?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Palau article.

questions.proof: It is sometimes referred to in English under its native name Belau.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Palau is 300 miles (500 km) east of the _____.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Palau article.

questions.proof: Palau is 300 miles (500 km) east of the Philippines.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “It got independence from United Nations trusteeship administration (administered by the United States of America) in _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Palau article.

questions.proof: It got independence from United Nations trusteeship administration (administered by the United States of America) in 1994.
